title: Expanded-bound chirped HfO2/SiO2 stack with hybrid initialization
scientific_hypothesis: Score regression resulted from overly restrictive thickness perturbation bounds that trapped optimization in a local minimum. Expanding bounds to ±15% on layers 1, 2, 7, 9 and implementing hybrid initialization (elite retention plus broad stochastic seeding) will restore search flexibility and improve target score.
design_principle: Chirped Bragg reflector architecture with alternating high/low index layers, optimized thicknesses for UV passband (255-280 nm) and visible/NIR stopbands (300-1100 nm). Critical interface layers (1, 2, 7, 9) require expanded tolerance to relieve compensatory strain.
proposed_topology: 11-layer fixed sequence: HfO2|SiO2|HfO2|SiO2|HfO2|SiO2|HfO2|SiO2|HfO2|SiO2|HfO2 on fused silica substrate, air incidence
design_variables: Perturbation bounds: ±15% on layers 1,2,7,9; ±10% on others
Hybrid initialization: 50% elite from prior best thicknesses, 50% stochastic ±20%
manufacturing_considerations: HfO2 and SiO2 are conventional depositable dielectrics
Thickness precision affected by expanded bounds
theory_basis: Chirped Bragg stack theory for broadband blocking
Local minimum escape via expanded search bounds
expected_advantages: Restored optimization flexibility compared to restrictive bounds
Potential to exceed prior peak scores
Maintains proven 11-layer topology while exploring new thickness regimes
known_risks: Expanded bounds may increase fabrication sensitivity
Hybrid initialization may slow convergence if stochastic seeds dominate
HfO2 absorption at deep UV wavelengths requires verification
execution_request_english: Optimize an 11-layer dielectric stack on fused silica substrate with air incidence. Layer sequence: HfO2|SiO2|HfO2|SiO2|HfO2|SiO2|HfO2|SiO2|HfO2|SiO2|HfO2. Thickness bounds: 20-150 nm for all layers. Perturbation bounds: ±15% for layers 1, 2, 7, 9; ±10% for layers 3, 4, 5, 6, 8, 10, 11. Initialization: hybrid scheme with 50% of candidates seeded from prior best-performing thicknesses (target_score > 0.38) and 50% randomly seeded with ±20% stochastic perturbation from nominal quarter-wave values at 267.5 nm center wavelength. Optimize for maximum transmittance in 255-280 nm band and minimum transmittance in 300-700 nm and 700-1100 nm bands. Use gradient_thickness and differential_evolution_thickness optimizers. Report best_target_score, valid_candidates, tightest_margin, and thicknesses_nm for all candidates. Canonical user controls: wavelength intervals 255-280 nm, 300-700 nm, 700-1100 nm. soft objectives: High transmittance in 255–280 nm. behaviors to suppress or avoid: Transmittance in 300–700 nm; Transmittance in 700–1100 nm. manufacturing constraints: Maximum 30 layers; No metal layers; Only conventional depositable inorganic dielectric materials.
revision_reason: Score regression attributed to overly restrictive ±2% bounds. This refinement expands bounds to ±15% on critical layers and implements hybrid initialization per feedback directive to escape local minima.
